script: Good morning, this is Stocksplain for Wednesday, November 18. Nvidia is leading the headlines today after reporting strong third-quarter earnings that beat analyst expectations. The company posted one hundred fifteen billion dollars in revenue, which is a one hundred three percent increase from a year ago. Despite this financial success, the company is moving forward without former leader Jensen Huang, as the board confirmed he will not return following investigations into his conduct. Investors are now watching closely to see how interim leadership manages the company's future roadmap and its strategy for financing smaller cloud providers. Meanwhile, the artificial intelligence sector is bracing for the upcoming Anthropic initial public offering. The company is expected to raise ninety billion dollars at a one point four trillion dollar valuation, with significant price support from major tech giants. This event will be a major test of market sentiment toward AI, though some analysts worry that the small five percent float could artificially prop up the share price. In other news, the Federal Aviation Administration has paused new system upgrades following a nationwide ground stop caused by a single router failure. This incident highlights the fragility of our critical digital infrastructure, as experts note that compounding technical debt in aging systems is creating more frequent cascading outages. Finally, we are seeing rising concerns about the massive debt being used to fund AI data centers. Hyperscalers have sold over one hundred thirty billion dollars in bonds so far this year to build out this infrastructure. Oracle, in particular, has seen its debt nearly double to one hundred sixty-nine billion dollars in just two years, shifting it from a cash-generating business to a capital-intensive one with a credit rating hovering just above junk status. Today's concept is circular financing. This happens when interconnected businesses invest in, lend to, or purchase goods from one another to generate activity within their own ecosystem. Instead of capital coming from independent end-users, money flows in a loop between allied vendors, developers, and infrastructure providers. While this mechanism can inflate reported demand, it also multiplies systemic risk. If end-user revenue fails to materialize, a default at one firm can destabilize all its interconnected partners. Understanding these hidden links is essential for any investor looking at the current AI boom. That is your briefing for today. Thanks for listening, and we will see you back here tomorrow.
